I am a 58-year-old farmer in Iringa with no schooling, but I have learned farming from my father and many seasons of experience. The soils here are good and the rains usually come, so maize grows well, though I still need to add fertilizer because the land gets tired after years of planting. I will use the government voucher to buy some chemical fertilizer, and I will also put cow manure because I keep some animals on my other land. I plant improved maize seed because it gives better yield than the local seed my grandfather used, but I do not buy chemicals for weeds or pests—weeding is done by hand with a hoe, and my family manages the work together. Since the rains in Iringa are reliable, I do not need to irrigate this plot.
